$comment: What RollView adds on top of the Tapio Design System, and nothing else.
`tapio-tokens.json` beside this file is the design system's own token file,
byte for byte. It is never edited here: `scripts/sync_design_system.py`
copies it in and records its hash below, so a value that has moved upstream
shows up as a failing test rather than as a colour that quietly disagrees
with Tapio Analysis.
Every entry here is an *addition*. Nothing in this file may restate or
override a value the system already authors — `test_theme_tokens.py` fails
if it does. Anything derivable from the system's own tokens is derived in
`theme/tokens.py` instead of being copied: the status palette, the
scatter-safe trio, the recency ramp and the dark sequential ramp are all
computed there.
The system's density scale, which RollView now carries whole rather than
flattening to the one row it runs at. `size.density` upstream authors the
row height and the cell padding; the control height and the base text
size are in the guide's density table and in the CSS and Qt exports but
not yet in the token file, so they are carried here until it grows them.
`default` is the row RollView starts in: a lab desktop with a mouse and a
keyboard. A mill-floor build changes this one word.
The system names one family per role. A desktop build also needs what to
fall back to on a machine where the bundled Plex faces failed to register
— an X session without fontconfig write access, a locked-down Windows
image. The Plex names come from the system and are prepended in code.
`preset` picks which column of the system's mark table is in force.
`screen` on a canvas in a window; `export` for anything written to a file
or the clipboard, so a figure is not thinner in print than on screen.
`supportingMark` is a weight the system does not author, for a chart it
does not specify: the individual profiles a mean is drawn from. They are
context rather than the subject, so they run below the series weight
(1.5 pt) without reaching the limit line's (1.2) or the dashed target's
(0.8) — neither of which is a data line. Same screen-to-export ratio as
the marks around it. Named separately rather than added to the system's
`chart.mark`, because that block is the system's to author.
